target_customer: Online stores and e-commerce brands that run discounts and promotions
problem: Stores give blanket discounts that waste margin; Cherry used AI to target and track dynamic promotions to new and existing customers.
business_model: B2B SaaS for e-commerce promotion management

founders.name: Isaac Donnelly
founders.background_notes: Startup Daily describes him as a former McKinsey engagement manager; YC page says project manager and now Director of AI at Optus.

founders.name: Rian Finnegan
previous_startups: An earlier startup that he shut down and returned money to investors (not named)
founders.background_notes: Software engineer. Met Donnelly as undergraduates at UNSW.

exit.reason: Rian Finnegan's YC bio says he shut down a startup and returned investors' money; it does not name the company, so the link to Cherry is likely but not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time targeting and promotion tracking needs store integrations and some modeling, standard applied ML for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Discount targeting sits on top of commerce platforms and could be copied by personalization suites or the platforms themselves.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in the sources read.

market_need_then: The company claimed conversion lifts of up to 51 percent for customers (a company claim), and Startup Daily named clients Vitable, Mosh and Phoria. No independent spend data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and plain on the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: Brand searches returned only unrelated Cherry companies, showing the name is generic and crowded in search; no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Cherry Recommends raised a US$500K seed from CP Ventures in mid-2021 and joined YC in Winter 2022, then went inactive. A founder bio indicates a shutdown with money returned to investors, but no post-mortem, press report or founder statement gives the cause, so the cause is not public.
notes: YC lists no website for this company, so there was no site to fetch. Funding: seed of US$500K from Startup Daily (Feb 2022); the YC amount of US$125K for 7 percent is from the same article. CB Insights (seen in a search summary) lists a US$0.5M convertible note dated 2022-02-07, which may be the same money as the seed or a separate note. A StartupIntros page cites a US$4M seed announced November 2022 that is probably another company with a similar name, so it is not recorded. Competitor search found no dated rivals; Promi turned out to be a 2024 YC company and was excluded. Startup Daily calls the company a Sydney startup while YC lists Singapore, and the 2020 founding is from YC.
